Unalive
un-uh-LYVE
verb / adjective (Gen-Z slang)
Algospeak from TikTok, c. 2020–2021. Creators who believed the platform removed or quietly suppressed videos containing kill, dead, or suicide substituted unalive (to kill, to die) and unalive myself (suicide). There were scattered jokey uses of the word before 2020, but the common sense is a moderation workaround. It spread to YouTube, true-crime and news-recap videos, and then off the screen into schools, where teachers report young children using it as an everyday word.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang unalive means kill or die, and unalive myself means suicide. It was made to slip past the filters on TikTok and YouTube, and it has since walked off the screen into classrooms, where children say it of video-game characters, of a strict teacher, and sometimes of themselves. The Christian observation: a softer word does not make a softer thing. God’s law names it plainly: "Thou shalt not kill" (Exo 20:13), and Genesis gives the reason: "for in the image of God made he man" (Gen 9:6). That commandment guards our own lives as well as our neighbour’s: "ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body" (1Co 6:20). When the jailer at Philippi drew his sword on himself, Paul did not lecture him; he "cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here" (Act 16:28), and before morning the man was baptised and rejoicing. That is the church’s whole posture toward the despairing: a loud cry, a near presence, and Christ. "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart" (Psa 34:18), and the Lord Jesus says, "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mat 11:28). Say this plainly to every parent: if your child uses this word about himself, even as a joke, take it seriously. Stop, ask him directly, listen, and get help that day — your pastor, your doctor, and, in the United States, the 988 crisis line or emergency services if there is any danger. A father tells his child: there is no darkness you can bring to us that will make us love you less, and no sin or sorrow too heavy for the Saviour who carried the cross. Your life is not yours to end; it is His to keep, and He keeps it gladly.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z algospeak (TikTok c. 2020–present) for kill, die, or suicide, coined to dodge moderation — a softened word for what the sixth commandment forbids, and a cry from a child that must always be heard.

expand to see more

UNALIVE, v.t. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2020–present; TikTok algospeak) To kill; unalive oneself, to commit suicide; unalived, killed or dead. "The main character gets unalived in the finale."

Forms: unaliving, unalive myself; common in news-recap and true-crime videos and in jokes; now heard in classrooms from young children who learned it online.

No settled older sense. A grandparent’s plain words for the same things are kill, die, and suicide — and plain words are better here.

Webster (1828), root word kill: “KILL, verb transitive 1. To deprive of life, animal or vegetable, in any manner or by any means. To kill an animal or a plant, is to put an end to the vital functions, either by destroying or essentially injuring the organs necessary to life, or by causing them to cease from action.”

Decode for parents: if your child says it about himself — even laughing — take it seriously. Ask him directly whether he has thought about ending his life, listen without panic, and get help the same day.

Key Scripture

Exo 20:13 — "Thou shalt not kill."

1Co 6:20 — "For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's."

Act 16:28 — "But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here."

Psa 34:18 — "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit."

Mat 11:28 — "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."

Modern Corruption

Unalive softens the words for killing and self-murder so they pass the filters, and in doing so makes the gravest things sayable as jokes, even by small children.

expand to see more

Euphemism is old; men have always found gentler words for death. What is new is a euphemism made for a machine. Unalive exists because platforms flag kill and suicide, so creators invented a word the software could not read. The result is a cartoon word for the darkest act there is, small enough for a seven-year-old to say on the playground. God does not soften it: "Thou shalt not kill" (Exo 20:13), "for in the image of God made he man" (Gen 9:6). The sixth commandment forbids taking our own life as surely as our neighbour’s, for "ye are bought with a price" (1Co 6:20).

But the church must hear what is underneath the word. Many children who say it are joking; some are not, and a joke is often how a frightened child tests whether anyone will notice. Notice. Paul’s cry to the despairing jailer, "Do thyself no harm: for we are all here" (Act 16:28), is the pattern for parents: a loud voice, a near presence, and then the gospel. The Lord Jesus came for the heavy laden (Mat 11:28) and is "nigh unto them that are of a broken heart" (Psa 34:18). Teach your children the plain words, and teach them that no despair is beyond His reach. If there is danger, get help now: your pastor, your doctor, and in the United States the 988 crisis line.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English on life → alive + un- (not) → c. 2020 TikTok algospeak: unalive, to kill, to die, suicide.
